---
title: "Get started with rthologs"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

rthologs looks up cross-species gene orthologs and returns a tidy R data frame.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub with pak.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pak::pak("igordot/rthologs")
```

Load rthologs to run the examples.

```{r setup}
library(rthologs)
```

## Orthologs

Use `orthologs()` to find the orthologs of a set of genes.
Give the genes, the source species of the genes, and the target species.

```{r}
odf <- orthologs("TP53", source = "human", target = "mouse")
odf
```

The result is a standard data frame with one row for each known ortholog of the input genes.
The `target_` columns identify the ortholog.

The source and target can be any two species in the package.

```{r}
odf <- orthologs("Trp53", source = "mouse", target = "rat")
odf
```

### Input genes

The input can be gene symbols, NCBI IDs, or Ensembl IDs.
Inputs are case-sensitive and you can mix the input types in one vector.

```{r}
genes <- c("TP53", "7157", "ENSG00000141510")
odf <- orthologs(genes, source = "human", target = "mouse")
odf
```

An input with no direct match can match a gene synonym.
To use only the primary names, set `synonyms = FALSE`.

```{r}
genes <- c("GAPDH", "CTGF", "SEPT7")
orthologs(genes, source = "human", target = "mouse")
```

```{r}
orthologs(genes, source = "human", target = "mouse", synonyms = FALSE)
```

### Output columns

Set `details = TRUE` to include the source gene IDs and the supporting methods.
The `support` and the `support_n`columns list the ortholog sources and their count.

```{r}
odf <- orthologs("TP53", source = "human", target = "mouse", details = TRUE)
dplyr::glimpse(odf)
```

### Multiple matches

An input can have more than one ortholog.
Each ortholog gets its own row.

```{r}
orthologs(genes = c("Ptprc", "Hba-a1", "Gapdh"), source = "mouse", target = "zebrafish")
```

By default, the result includes only the best matches.
To get all the potential orthologs, set `best = FALSE`.

```{r}
odf <- orthologs(
  "Hba-a1",
  source = "mouse",
  target = "zebrafish",
  best = FALSE,
  details = TRUE
)
odf[, c("input", "target_symbol", "support_n")]
```

Set `min_support` to keep pairs with a certain number of supporting methods.

```{r}
odf <- orthologs(
  "Hba-a1",
  source = "mouse",
  target = "zebrafish",
  best = FALSE,
  min_support = 6,
  details = TRUE
)
odf[, c("input", "target_symbol", "support_n")]
```

### Inputs without orthologs

By default, the output only includes genes with known orthologs.
To keep all inputs, set `orthologs_only = FALSE`.

```{r}
orthologs(
  genes = c("Ptprc", "Cd34", "Fakegene"),
  source = "mouse",
  target = "zebrafish",
  orthologs_only = FALSE
)
```

Genes without orthologs get one row with `NA` in all columns.
`Cd34` is a valid mouse gene, but the data contain no zebrafish ortholog for it.
`Fakegene` is not a mouse gene.

## Species

Use `species()` to list the available species and their accepted names.

```{r}
species()
```

## Data

The orthologs come from the [Alliance of Genome Resources](https://www.alliancegenome.org/) (AGR).
AGR combines predictions from these sources: PANTHER, SonicParanoid, OrthoFinder, Ensembl Compara, OrthoInspector, InParanoid, PhylomeDB, OMA, Hieranoid, HGNC, and ZFIN.

The package uses the AGR stringent set that includes:

* Pairs that three or more methods support, with a best match in at least one direction.
* Pairs that two methods support, with a best match in both directions.
* All pairs from HGNC or ZFIN.

If you use the data, please cite:
Alliance of Genome Resources Consortium.
Updates to the Alliance of Genome Resources central infrastructure. *Genetics*. 2024.
doi: [10.1093/genetics/iyae049](https://doi.org/10.1093/genetics/iyae049).
